## Primer (read before you watch)

**What you'll learn:** the 3 pillars that make up AJO's value, the 3 personas who use it day to
day, and a tour of the homepage/left-nav so the UI isn't a surprise when you log in.

**Key concepts:**
- **3 value drivers:** *Real-time customer insights & engagement* — Real-Time Customer Profile
  (RTCP) fuses live data from every touchpoint into a 360° profile and moves customers in/out of
  segments and journeys live, not just via static lists. *Modern omnichannel orchestration* — one
  Journey Canvas for both batch campaigns and real-time 1:1 interactions, plus a drag-and-drop
  Message Designer and an embedded lightweight asset library. *Intelligent decisioning &
  personalization* — Decision Management (a centralized offer library + eligibility rules) plus
  AI/ML for send-time optimization and predictive engagement scoring.
- **3 personas, one app:** **Marketer/Business Practitioner** (builds journeys, campaigns,
  audiences, offers, creative), **Data Architect/Engineer** (models schemas, sets up source
  connectors/ingestion), **Admin** (manages permissions, sandboxes, channel setup). Smaller orgs
  often combine these into fewer people — but the left nav is organized around this 3-way split.
- **No tool-switching:** everything for an end-to-end use case — profile data, orchestration, and
  decisioning — lives inside one app.

**Common mistakes to avoid:** treating AJO as "just an email tool" (it's channel-agnostic
orchestration + decisioning, not a single-channel sender); assuming one person needs to own all 3
personas' work, when in most orgs these are separate roles/teams.

**Where it fits the spine:** this is the 30,000-ft view before the rest of Foundation goes layer by
layer through Ingest → Model → Identity → Profile → Segment → Activate → Orchestrate. Everything
after this topic is "how do I actually build one of these 3 pillars."
